There’s a bit of a “speed‐ranking” puzzle here. When people talk about the “fastest birds” they often list the Peregrine Falcon (whose dive can exceed 389 km/h) as number one and the Golden Eagle (with dives around 320 km/h) as number two. For level (non‐diving) flight the record is held by the White‐throated Needletail, which has been clocked at about 169 km/h. (Some sources mention the Common Swift as “the fastest bird in level flight” with speeds around 111 km/h, but more recent measurements show the Needletail is even faster.) 

So if you rank by maximum airspeed overall (whether diving or level flight), the top three are usually taken to be:
 1. Peregrine Falcon – ~389 km/h (in a dive)
 2. Golden Eagle – ~320 km/h (in a dive)
 3. White‐throated Needletail – ~169 km/h (in level flight)

That makes the third fastest bird the White‐throated Needletail, with a maximum airspeed of about 169 km/h.

Keep in mind that “maximum airspeed” can be measured in different ways (diving speed versus level flight speed), but under the common ranking the answer is 169 km/h.
